content.title: Open the concentration warning popover

check.operand: a visible concentration warning popover anchored to the warning

content.test_md_blob:
# Open the concentration warning popover

> Prove the interactive warning reveals the anchored popover with the concentration details and recommended action.

## Step 1

Open {{start_url}} and arrive at the portfolio dashboard section headed "Portfolio Risk".

## Step 2

In the Portfolio Risk section, locate the visible concentration warning that reads "Risk concentration detected" and "Technology exposure exceeds target by 4.2%", then activate that warning.

## Step 3

Assert the warning popover anchored to the concentration warning is visible and shows the heading "TECHNOLOGY OVERWEIGHT", Current allocation 31.7%, Target 27.5%, Deviation +4.2%, and the recommended action "Review sector concentration.".

## Step 4 — assert @verifies ac-81, ac-82, ac-83, ac-84, ac-85, ac-86, ac-71, ac-72

Confirm presence check: a visible concentration warning popover anchored to the warning (exists) — the stated promise: Activating the interactive concentration warning reveals a popover anchored to the warning.

    step: 2
  - objective: Assert the warning popover anchored to the concentration warning is visible and shows the heading "TECHNOLOGY OVERWEIGHT", Current allocation 31.7%, Target 27.5%, Deviation +4.2%, and the recommended action "Review sector concentration.".

content.title: Dismiss the warning popover by clicking elsewhere
content.test_md_blob:
# Dismiss the warning popover by clicking elsewhere

> Prove the warning popover closes when a pointer interaction occurs outside the warning and its anchored popover.

## Step 1

Open {{start_url}} and arrive at the portfolio dashboard section headed "Portfolio Risk".

## Step 2

In the Portfolio Risk section, activate the visible concentration warning so its anchored popover opens.

## Step 3

Store the warning popover visibility state as baseline_popover_state after the popover opens; confirm the current state is open.

## Step 4

Click in a neutral area of the portfolio dashboard outside both the warning and the anchored popover.

## Step 5

Assert the concentration warning popover is no longer visible.

## Step 6 — assert @verifies ac-87

Confirm state-transition check: closed (equals) — the stated promise: After clicking elsewhere, the warning popover changes from open to closed.

content.title: Review default portfolio risk status and warning signal
content.test_md_blob:
# Review default portfolio risk status and warning signal

> Prove the default dashboard view exposes the risk metrics, gauge state, and visible concentration warning before any interaction.

## Step 1

Open {{start_url}} and arrive at the portfolio dashboard section headed "Portfolio Risk".

## Step 2

In the Portfolio Risk section, assert the risk gauge legend shows LOW, MODERATE, and HIGH, the current gauge value is 61, and the displayed status is MODERATE.

## Step 3

Assert the metrics list shows Volatility 14.82%, Sharpe 1.74, Beta 0.93, Max Drawdown -6.21%, and VaR 95% -2.48%.

## Step 4

Assert the concentration warning is visible with the headline "Risk concentration detected" and the detail "Technology exposure exceeds target by 4.2%".

## Step 5 — assert @verifies ac-71, ac-72, ac-73, ac-74, ac-75, ac-76, ac-77, ac-78, ac-79, ac-80

Confirm presence check: a displayed risk status of "MODERATE" (exists) — the stated promise: The risk monitor displays the current risk status as "MODERATE".

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Kept first because this pair proves the core interactive disclosure of the concentration warning and the actionable details the user investigates.
[value_score] Kept second because outside-click dismissal is explicitly required by the source and is a common interaction failure point for anchored popovers.
[value_score] Kept third because Escape dismissal is explicitly required and is the only grounded keyboard-driven interaction in the cited behavior.
[value_score] Kept fourth because it proves the default baseline risk data and visible warning signal, but its risk is lower than the interactive warning behaviors.

[self_critique] Oracle-proves-promise check passed: the primary check proves the popover becomes visible, and the assertion step narrows the scope to the exact heading, values, and recommended action grounded in ac-82 through ac-86.

[self_critique] Technique-fit check passed: state-transition oracles fit both dismissal paths because the source promised a change from open popover state to closed state after a specific user action.

[self_critique] Negative-case sweep found no grounded negative scenario to add without inventing behavior. The source specified disclosure and dismissal behaviors only, so I did not fabricate invalid-input or failure paths.

[self_critique] Over-breadth check passed with caution: the steps group only tightly related baseline display assertions within the same Portfolio Risk section, and the primary oracle stays narrow by binding the formal check to the displayed MODERATE status rather than a broad whole-page claim.
